deprecation_criterion: Superseded by the next safety-governance housekeep wave's baseline; single-use measured-reduction reference for this doc-slim wave.
description: Post-wave line-count FLOOR for safety-governance doc surfaces. Originally captured at commit 7a42f9c (before the housekeep measured doc-reduction wave) at spec.md=261; the housekeep e2e test asserts the current docs are STRICTLY smaller than this floor and that load-bearing tokens survived the slim. The floor was RAISED from 261 to 268 by the additive work_own_filings knob (schema 2.2.0, §3.11.5 default-on opt-out): an additive feature legitimately documents one new knob in spec.md. The floor was RAISED AGAIN from 269 to 281 by the additive #337 default-resolution paragraph (load_config reads the shipped default-config/config.json FRESH when no project-local config exists, else DEFAULT_GOVERNANCE): an additive feature legitimately documents its new resolution rule in spec.md. The floor was LOWERED from 281 to 280 by the #346 measured doc-reduction wave, which removed one proven-redundant restatement (the Backoff/§3.8.5 DEFERRED paragraph in the Merge guardrails section, fully restated in the Deferred section — the §3.8.5 citation survives at the backoff.threshold field and the Deferred entry): spec.md is now 275, strictly below the re-anchored floor, and every load-bearing token survived. The floor was RAISED AGAIN from 280 to 293 by the additive regression_command knob (schema 2.5.0): the GATE full-regression shell command read by verify-integrate, documented as one new config field (JSON example line + describing bullet) in spec.md, which grew it to 287 — an additive feature legitimately documents its new knob. The floor was RAISED AGAIN from 293 to 303 by the additive field-level (3-way) config merge (#357, deferred #336): merge_config unfreezes an overridden config.json so it adopts new default keys while preserving user values and surfacing conflicts, documented as one new resolution paragraph in spec.md, which grew it to 297 — an additive feature legitimately documents its new resolution rule. The floor was RAISED AGAIN from 303 to 311 by the additive doc_check_features_root knob (schema 2.6.0, #381): a repo-relative features root the verify-integrate GATE's doc-surface load-bearing-token check uses, kept separate from features_root so the doc gate is opt-in independently and LIVE on the auto-merge path, documented as one new config field (JSON example line + describing bullet) in spec.md, which grew it to 304 — an additive feature legitimately documents its new knob. The floor was RAISED AGAIN from 311 to 351 by the additive issue_filter knob (schema 2.6.0 -> 2.7.0): the PULL-stage open-issue filter (a DNF label matcher + a title_pattern regex) read + normalized through the pure accessor issue_filter(config), documented as one new config field (JSON example block + describing bullet list + an Invariants bullet) in spec.md, which grew it to 344 — an additive feature legitimately documents its new knob. The floor was RAISED AGAIN from 351 to 411 by the Phase 2 configure-writer + guided --setup onboarding expansion (schema UNCHANGED at 2.7.0 — writer-only): the 'Config writer + the configure skill' section documents the new configure.py surface (--features-root, --work-own-filings, --issue-labels, --issue-title-pattern, the read-only --preflight gh probe, and the --describe per-knob loop-'stage' ordering) and the rewritten 5-step guided --setup onboarding, which grew spec.md to 404 — a writer-only feature expansion legitimately documents its new CLI surface and onboarding flow in spec.md. The gate still guards against re-bloating below the floor; contract.md is unchanged. The floor was RAISED AGAIN from 411 to 438 by the additive implement_test_command knob (schema 2.7.0 -> 2.8.0): the IMPLEMENT-side per-work-order test-gate command read through the pure accessor implement_test_command(config) (null = run <feature>/test/run.py, a command string = run it, the sentinel 'none'/'skip' = skip the gate), documented as one new config field (JSON example line + a describing bullet + the --describe IMPLEMENT-stage ordering) in spec.md, which grew it to 431 — an additive feature legitimately documents its new knob. The floor was RAISED AGAIN from 438 to 454 by the additive schema_version field-merge-exclusion paragraph (noise fix): schema_version is loader-owned metadata EXCLUDED from the 3-way field-merge so no spurious 'field-merge conflict at schema_version' warning is emitted (it is already normalized to GOVERNANCE_SCHEMA_VERSION by _overlay), documented as one new resolution paragraph in spec.md, which grew it to 447 — a legitimate documentation of the loader's field-merge exclusion rule. The floor was RAISED AGAIN from 454 to 468 by the additive issue_filter_apply_labels(config) accessor (schema UNCHANGED at 2.8.0 — accessor only, no new config field): the pure helper returning the FIRST non-empty AND-group of the normalized issue_filter.labels (the labels a loop-FILED discovery issue must carry to be re-pullable by a later label-filtered PULL; [] when no filter), documented as one new sub-bullet under the issue_filter field in spec.md, which grew it to 461 — an additive accessor legitimately documents its behavior in spec.md. The floor was RAISED AGAIN from 468 to 486 by the additive issue_filter.exclude_labels term (schema 2.7.0 -> 2.8.0): the flat OR of forbidden labels an open issue must NOT carry (a NEGATIVE term applied post-fetch by work-intake PULL — how a disposed auto-maintainer-rejected reject is kept out of PULL), read + canonicalized through the same issue_filter(config) normalizer and settable via the new --issue-exclude-labels configure flag, documented as one new JSON example line + a describing bullet + an Invariants clause in spec.md, which grew it to 479 — an additive feature legitimately documents its new knob.
